question: Does a Layer-1 admission filter change candidate availability on this engine?

comparator.build: unattributed; the artifact carries no engine_version
comparator.note: The historical result stands for the build that produced it. Its seed block is consumed and is not reused here.

design.world: generate_compositional_world(seed, cycles), the Gate 13 world, identical for both arms of a seed
design.pairing: both arms of a seed run on the same generated world; only service_cls differs
design.adopted_arm: DiversityFirstSleepService, restored in-process from the definition at a82e890 because the module was removed at withdrawal

seeds.freshness: the first contiguous window of nine integers at or above 20510101 that appears in no file under docs, tests, benchmarks, research-journal or papers; the ninth is the bootstrap seed and is not a world seed

criteria.bar_rule: mean paired coverage difference (adopted minus reference) at or above the bar, interval lower bound above zero, and at least seven of eight seeds with a positive difference
criteria.bar_provenance: carried as policy from the original ADMISSION-TWO-ARM-1 registration: one half of the order block's measured mean delta, 0.1615, floored to two decimals; it is not calibrated on this layer
criteria.guard_rule: mean paired precision difference (adopted minus reference) at or above the guard bar
criteria.guard_provenance: declared, not calibrated: 0.05 is the smallest difference this project's instruments have been asked to distinguish

decision_table.condition: gates pass; gain passes; guard passes
decision_table.reading: the restored adopted admission covers more of the world's edges at the same budget without losing precision

decision_table.condition: gates pass; gain passes; guard fails
decision_table.reading: coverage rises and precision falls; the trade is recorded and nothing is claimed as a gain

decision_table.condition: gates pass; gain fails; interval width at or below 0.30
decision_table.reading: the adopted rule does not cover more of the world here; the historical negative answer survives

decision_table.condition: gates pass; gain fails; interval width above 0.30
decision_table.reading: the interval cannot place the difference; absence of a gain is not established
reported as the gate, never as a gain or a loss

classification.SURVIVED: the re-derived verdict is NO GAIN ON THIS LAYER, matching the historical answer
classification.REVERSED: the re-derived verdict is ADOPTED ARM GAINS
classification.CHANGED: the re-derived verdict is PRICED TRADE
classification.NOT_MEASURABLE: the re-derived verdict is UNDERPOWERED or VOID

gates.G0_liveness: the two arms' asserted fingerprints must differ on at least seven of eight seeds
gates.G1_world_present: raw temporal coverage must be 1.0 in both arms of every seed
gates.G2_arithmetic: covered cannot exceed asserted; coverage and precision must equal their stated ratios
gates.G3_determinism: the reference arm re-run on the first seed must produce the same asserted fingerprint
gates.G4_denominator: the world must have at least one compositional edge in every seed
gates.G5_boundary: no frozen engine file may differ from HEAD when the block runs

not_evidence: This is one world family at one horizon and one cap. It says whether the historical admission answer survives on 0.13.0; it does not establish that diversity-first ordering is wrong anywhere else.
